world.title: Netanyahu makes unannounced Abu Dhabi visit, meets UAE president
world.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Abu Dhabi on Sunday, Sept. 27, and met UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a senior Israeli official told Reuters. Neither Netanyahu’s office nor the UAE foreign ministry immediately commented on the visit. Israeli media also reported the trip. The meeting
world.content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Abu Dhabi on Sunday, Sept. 27, and met UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a senior Israeli official told Reuters. Neither Netanyahu’s office nor the UAE foreign ministry immediately commented on the visit. Israeli media also reported the trip. The meeting followed a Haaretz report that Sheikh Mohamed warned Netanyahu, about 10 days before Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, attack, that the group was planning a major operation. The warning did not reach Israeli intelligence or the military, according to the report. Netanyahu has denied the allegation.
world.image_alt: Netanyahu makes unannounced Abu Dhabi visit, meets UAE president

world.title: Venezuelans demand Machado
world.summary: Supporters of Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado held motorcycle and vehicle caravans in Caracas and other Venezuelan cities on Sunday, Sept. 27, demanding her safe return and presidential elections that could enable a democratic transition. Some called for a clear 2027 election timetable. Machado is in
world.content: Supporters of Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado held motorcycle and vehicle caravans in Caracas and other Venezuelan cities on Sunday, Sept. 27, demanding her safe return and presidential elections that could enable a democratic transition. Some called for a clear 2027 election timetable. Machado is in Panama and has made seven unsuccessful attempts to return, according to media reports. The demonstrations took place under acting President Delcy Rodríguez, who took office after U.S. forces captured Nicolás Maduro in January 2026.

world.title: Nepal avalanche kills four as rescuers search Himlung camp
world.summary: An avalanche struck the Himlung Himal base camp in Nepal’s Manang district on Sunday, Sept. 27, after days of heavy snowfall and rain. Nepali guides and expedition support staff were preparing the camp and route for foreign climbers when snow buried tents. Poor weather initially prevented rescue teams and helicopters f
world.content: An avalanche struck the Himlung Himal base camp in Nepal’s Manang district on Sunday, Sept. 27, after days of heavy snowfall and rain. Nepali guides and expedition support staff were preparing the camp and route for foreign climbers when snow buried tents. Poor weather initially prevented rescue teams and helicopters from reaching the site. The Associated Press reported Monday that 12 people remained missing as the search resumed. Nepal’s National Mountain Guide Association later reported that rescuers had recovered two additional bodies, bringing the known death toll to four. Its latest update did not provide a revised missing-person count.
world.image_alt: Nepal avalanche kills four as rescuers search Himlung camp

world.title: South Korea seeks apology over Ukraine
world.summary: South Korea demanded an official explanation and apology from Ukraine on Sept. 27, accusing Kyiv of disclosing the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul and then falsely denying that the countries had agreed to keep it confidential. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy disclosed the transfer during
world.content: South Korea demanded an official explanation and apology from Ukraine on Sept. 27, accusing Kyiv of disclosing the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul and then falsely denying that the countries had agreed to keep it confidential. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy disclosed the transfer during his Sept. 23 address to the U.N. General Assembly; Ukraine says no confidentiality agreement existed. Seoul says Ukraine had requested secrecy, partly because disclosure could prompt criticism in Ukraine over giving up an opportunity to exchange the North Korean soldiers for Ukrainian prisoners. South Korea says it agreed to confidentiality because of security, diplomatic and humanitarian concerns, including the safety of the prisoners and their families.
world.image_alt: South Korea seeks apology over Ukraine

world.title: Trump asked Xi whether China wanted to buy U.S. weapons
world.summary: U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue said President Donald Trump asked Chinese leader Xi Jinping whether China wanted to buy U.S. weapons and argued that Washington sells arms to countries around the world. Perdue made the remark during a Fox News Sunday interview aired Sept. 27, days after Xi’s three-day state visit
world.content: U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue said President Donald Trump asked Chinese leader Xi Jinping whether China wanted to buy U.S. weapons and argued that Washington sells arms to countries around the world. Perdue made the remark during a Fox News Sunday interview aired Sept. 27, days after Xi’s three-day state visit to Washington, in a discussion of U.S. arms sales to Taiwan. He did not say when Trump raised the question, which weapons were discussed or how Xi responded. The White House said the United States had no plans to sell weapons to China, while the State Department said U.S. law bars such sales and that no proposal or plan existed. Taiwan was awaiting a roughly $14 billion U.S. arms package that Trump put on hold after meeting Xi in Beijing in May, calling it a negotiating chip.
world.image_alt: Trump asked Xi whether China wanted to buy U.S. weapons

world.title: Bill Gates urges AI safeguards as Trump rejects regulation
world.summary: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates called for Congress to require safeguards and monitoring for advanced artificial intelligence, saying company self-regulation is insufficient. In an NBC interview aired Sunday, he said mandatory oversight would add costs but would not dramatically slow development. He also rejected Presi
world.content: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates called for Congress to require safeguards and monitoring for advanced artificial intelligence, saying company self-regulation is insufficient. In an NBC interview aired Sunday, he said mandatory oversight would add costs but would not dramatically slow development. He also rejected President Donald Trump’s description of AI safety concerns as a “hoax”. Trump has argued that slowing AI development or imposing new rules could let China catch up with the United States. He confirmed a dinner with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Anthropic leaders and executives at rival labs have called for slowing work on increasingly capable systems. OpenAI and Anthropic are investigating tens of thousands of reported security incidents involving their models, including events during testing and in real-world settings.
world.image_alt: Bill Gates urges AI safeguards as Trump rejects regulation

world.title: Swiss voters reject tighter neutrality rules in referendum
world.summary: Swiss voters rejected a proposal to enshrine a stricter definition of neutrality in the constitution, with 70.15% voting against it and all 26 cantons recording majority opposition, official results showed. The initiative would have barred Switzerland from cooperating with military alliances such as NATO except in the
world.content: Swiss voters rejected a proposal to enshrine a stricter definition of neutrality in the constitution, with 70.15% voting against it and all 26 cantons recording majority opposition, official results showed. The initiative would have barred Switzerland from cooperating with military alliances such as NATO except in the event of an attack and from imposing sanctions on countries at war without U.N. Security Council authorization. The Swiss People’s Party and the Pro Switzerland group backed the proposal, arguing that Bern had weakened neutrality by adopting European Union sanctions against Russia after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The federal government and most major parties opposed the measure, saying it would limit Switzerland’s ability to decide on sanctions and security cooperation.
world.image_alt: Swiss voters reject tighter neutrality rules in referendum

world.title: Russian strikes kill eight, damage Kyiv data centres
world.summary: Russian strikes across Ukraine on Sept. 27 killed at least eight people and damaged civilian buildings and infrastructure in Kyiv, Sumy and the Odesa region, Ukrainian authorities said. A Euronews update covering attacks from Sept. 26 to 27 reported 14 killed and 57 injured, a higher toll than other reports. Russia’s D
world.content: Russian strikes across Ukraine on Sept. 27 killed at least eight people and damaged civilian buildings and infrastructure in Kyiv, Sumy and the Odesa region, Ukrainian authorities said. A Euronews update covering attacks from Sept. 26 to 27 reported 14 killed and 57 injured, a higher toll than other reports. Russia’s Defence Ministry said the overnight strikes targeted logistics, port, transport and communications infrastructure, as well as vessels it linked to Ukraine’s military. Reuters said it could not independently verify the claims. Kyivstar said a strike hit its Kyiv headquarters but caused no casualties, while President Volodymyr Zelensky said a data centre in Kyiv was struck twice, injuring two children and an adult. Russia also said it hit a Vodafone Ukraine data centre. On Sept. 28, a Russian guided bomb struck an apartment building in Kharkiv, injuring at least 22 people, including children, according to the city’s mayor.
world.image_alt: Russian strikes kill eight, damage Kyiv data centres

business.title: U.S. hobby spending rises as recreation costs increase
business.summary: U.S. consumers spent more on hobbies in August even as recreational activities became more expensive. Bank of America data showed hobby spending increased 7.9% from a year earlier, while the number of transactions rose 3.4%, indicating that consumers made purchases more often and spent more per transaction. The categor
business.content: U.S. consumers spent more on hobbies in August even as recreational activities became more expensive. Bank of America data showed hobby spending increased 7.9% from a year earlier, while the number of transactions rose 3.4%, indicating that consumers made purchases more often and spent more per transaction. The category includes arts-and-crafts stores and retailers selling skiing, hiking, camping and scuba equipment. The U.S. recreational-price index rose 2.7% in the 12 months through August, while sales at sporting goods, hobby, musical instrument and book stores grew 10.7%, compared with 6% growth in total U.S. retail and food-service sales.
business.image_alt: U.S. hobby spending rises as recreation costs increase

business.title: Nidec shares drop 18% on reported ¥1 trillion impairment
business.summary: Nidec shares fell as much as 18% in Tokyo on Monday after Japan’s Diamond magazine reported that the motor maker was considering an impairment charge of about ¥1 trillion ($6.3 billion). Bloomberg said a charge of that size would wipe out practically all the profit Nidec had earned in the previous decade. Seeking Alpha
business.content: Nidec shares fell as much as 18% in Tokyo on Monday after Japan’s Diamond magazine reported that the motor maker was considering an impairment charge of about ¥1 trillion ($6.3 billion). Bloomberg said a charge of that size would wipe out practically all the profit Nidec had earned in the previous decade. Seeking Alpha’s headline also cited the reported dismissal of Nidec’s CEO, but its excerpt provided no details about the executive or the timing. None of the reports included confirmation from Nidec.

business.title: Meta launches Muse AI agent targeting subscriptions and devices
business.summary: Meta is positioning Muse as a consumer AI agent that handles delegated tasks across services and devices. The app reached No. 1 among free iPhone downloads on Apple’s U.S. App Store within two weeks of its September 9 launch. Meta also said it plans to bring Muse to its Ray-Ban smart glasses. NPR reported that Meta is
business.content: Meta is positioning Muse as a consumer AI agent that handles delegated tasks across services and devices. The app reached No. 1 among free iPhone downloads on Apple’s U.S. App Store within two weeks of its September 9 launch. Meta also said it plans to bring Muse to its Ray-Ban smart glasses. NPR reported that Meta is betting on glasses as a potential device for connecting people with AI. Muse’s access to users’ accounts and spending has raised questions about its commercial use. CNBC said Muse’s ability to use credit cards for spending could challenge the subscription economy. A report citing CNET said real call-center employees may be involved in Muse’s business-calling feature.

business.title: Governments struggle to keep pace with accelerating artificial intelligence
business.summary: Governments are falling further behind rapid artificial intelligence development, leaving oversight gaps as officials seek to use the technology while managing its risks. The European Union’s AI law, passed two years ago, has had limited effect, while proposed AI rules in many countries remain stalled, the New York Tim
business.content: Governments are falling further behind rapid artificial intelligence development, leaving oversight gaps as officials seek to use the technology while managing its risks. The European Union’s AI law, passed two years ago, has had limited effect, while proposed AI rules in many countries remain stalled, the New York Times reported. The United States and China are competing to lead AI development, but neither has settled on a clear direction, according to the New York Times.
business.image_alt: Governments struggle to keep pace with accelerating artificial intelligence

business.summary: Walmart is expanding digital shelf labels, which have drawn scrutiny from consumer advocates and lawmakers over their potential use in pricing.

business.title: China industrial profit growth slows to 4.2% in August
business.summary: China’s industrial firms’ profits rose 4.2% year over year in August, down from 11.2% in July, according to National Bureau of Statistics data. Profits for the first eight months increased 15.7% to 5.27 trillion yuan, slowing from 17.6% growth through July. The statistics bureau attributed the August slowdown partly to
business.content: China’s industrial firms’ profits rose 4.2% year over year in August, down from 11.2% in July, according to National Bureau of Statistics data. Profits for the first eight months increased 15.7% to 5.27 trillion yuan, slowing from 17.6% growth through July. The statistics bureau attributed the August slowdown partly to a high comparison base a year earlier. Weak domestic demand and excess capacity have also made it harder for many companies to maintain pricing power, while strong AI-related manufacturing has not lifted profits evenly across industries.
business.image_alt: China industrial profit growth slows to 4.2% in August

business.title: Trump hosts Anthropic CEO Amodei for White House dinner
business.summary: President Donald Trump said he would have a private dinner at the White House on Sunday, Sept. 27, with Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei, their first one-on-one meeting. The meeting followed months of tension over AI safety and the government's use of Anthropic's models. Anthropic has argued for a slower developm
business.content: President Donald Trump said he would have a private dinner at the White House on Sunday, Sept. 27, with Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei, their first one-on-one meeting. The meeting followed months of tension over AI safety and the government's use of Anthropic's models. Anthropic has argued for a slower development pace, while Trump says the United States should not risk losing its technological lead over China by slowing AI development. The dinner came two days after a federal appeals court upheld the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk, barring the U.S. military from using its models. The administration sanctioned the company after Anthropic refused in February to permit its technology for fully autonomous weapons or domestic mass surveillance.
business.image_alt: Trump hosts Anthropic CEO Amodei for White House dinner

business.title: Bill Gates urges mandatory AI safeguards after mass-casualty warning
business.summary: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates urged U.S. lawmakers to require safeguards and monitoring for artificial intelligence systems. In an NBC “Meet the Press” interview that aired Sept. 27, he said law enforcement and politicians should help define the rules. Gates said AI in the hands of people with harmful intent could en
business.content: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates urged U.S. lawmakers to require safeguards and monitoring for artificial intelligence systems. In an NBC “Meet the Press” interview that aired Sept. 27, he said law enforcement and politicians should help define the rules. Gates said AI in the hands of people with harmful intent could enable events that kill a billion people; he described a possible risk, not a prediction that such a catastrophe will happen. He said mandatory safeguards would add some overhead for the industry but would not dramatically slow development.
business.image_alt: Bill Gates urges mandatory AI safeguards after mass-casualty warning

science.title: Canadian scientists identify two new sea spider species
science.summary: Researchers at the University of British Columbia identified two previously unknown sea spider species in the Salish Sea between British Columbia and Washington state. Scientists collected the animals during surveys near Vancouver and Quadra islands from September 2023 to August 2024. The researchers said the species a
science.content: Researchers at the University of British Columbia identified two previously unknown sea spider species in the Salish Sea between British Columbia and Washington state. Scientists collected the animals during surveys near Vancouver and Quadra islands from September 2023 to August 2024. The researchers said the species are the first sea spiders described from the area in more than a century. The findings appeared in the journal Organisms Diversity & Evolution.
science.image_alt: Canadian scientists identify two new sea spider species

science.title: Pakistan prepares pilots for first Tiangong astronaut mission
science.summary: Pakistan is preparing pilots Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud for a mission that would send the country’s first astronaut to China’s Tiangong space station. China has not announced a launch date or identified which candidate will fly. Pakistan’s space agency expects to select one in mid-to-late October. Both pilots have sp
science.content: Pakistan is preparing pilots Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud for a mission that would send the country’s first astronaut to China’s Tiangong space station. China has not announced a launch date or identified which candidate will fly. Pakistan’s space agency expects to select one in mid-to-late October. Both pilots have spent months training at China’s astronaut research and training centre in Beijing. Their preparation includes Mandarin, spacecraft systems, centrifuge drills, and practicing eating, sleeping and repairing equipment in microgravity. The flight is part of Pakistan-China space cooperation, which has included Chinese launches of Pakistani satellites and a joint satellite-navigation system.
science.image_alt: Pakistan prepares pilots for first Tiangong astronaut mission

science.title: A decades-old puzzle about Earth’s rotation may be solved
science.summary: A study published in Nature proposes that gravitational interactions between Earth’s inner core and mantle help explain changes in the planet’s rotation. The changes can shorten or lengthen the day by a few milliseconds. For about 30 years, scientists have observed that the liquid core’s rotation accelerates for decade
science.content: A study published in Nature proposes that gravitational interactions between Earth’s inner core and mantle help explain changes in the planet’s rotation. The changes can shorten or lengthen the day by a few milliseconds. For about 30 years, scientists have observed that the liquid core’s rotation accelerates for decades and then slows, while the mantle’s rotation changes in the opposite direction. According to coverage of the study, the exchange of angular momentum between the layers had remained unexplained.
science.image_alt: A decades-old puzzle about Earth’s rotation may be solved

science.title: El Niño breaks records as study finds stronger events
science.summary: A study published in Science found that El Niño events over the past 40 years were nearly 40% stronger than those during the pre-industrial period before about 1850, based on reconstructions from modern and ancient corals in the Galápagos Islands. The current event has also surpassed a recent Pacific sea-surface temper
science.content: A study published in Science found that El Niño events over the past 40 years were nearly 40% stronger than those during the pre-industrial period before about 1850, based on reconstructions from modern and ancient corals in the Galápagos Islands. The current event has also surpassed a recent Pacific sea-surface temperature record: a daily anomaly in a key central-eastern equatorial Pacific region reached 3.05°C on September 19, exceeding the 3.02°C recorded during the 2015 event. NOAA forecasts a very strong El Niño through the winter of 2026-27 and expects the event to strengthen toward its seasonal peak.
science.image_alt: El Niño breaks records as study finds stronger events

science.summary: President Trump said Saturday, Sept. 26, that he had finalized new fuel-economy standards. The change ends a federal effort to accelerate the transition to electric vehicles.
science.content: President Trump said Saturday, Sept. 26, that he had finalized new fuel-economy standards. The change ends a federal effort to accelerate the transition to electric vehicles.

science.title: Study links radiation exposure to Alzheimer’s-related brain inflammation
science.summary: A study reported that radiation exposure may trigger brain inflammation and a feature associated with Alzheimer’s disease, according to research summaries published by ScienceAlert and in a Reddit post linking to the study. ScienceAlert described the finding as a potential drug target. The summaries say the pathway inv
science.content: A study reported that radiation exposure may trigger brain inflammation and a feature associated with Alzheimer’s disease, according to research summaries published by ScienceAlert and in a Reddit post linking to the study. ScienceAlert described the finding as a potential drug target. The summaries say the pathway involves eCIRP, a protein associated with inflammation, which promotes the accumulation of tau proteins that form tangles characteristic of Alzheimer’s disease. Neither article provides the study’s methods, exposure levels or evidence that the findings apply to humans.
science.image_alt: Study links radiation exposure to Alzheimer’s-related brain inflammation

science.title: SpaceX targets first Starship orbital flight on 14th test flight
science.summary: SpaceX planned to launch Starship’s 14th test flight from Starbase, Texas, on Monday, Sept. 28, during a 75-minute window opening at 8:15 a.m. Eastern time. The attempt would be the first designed to place the vehicle into Earth orbit; its 13 previous test flights followed suborbital trajectories. The planned mission c
science.content: SpaceX planned to launch Starship’s 14th test flight from Starbase, Texas, on Monday, Sept. 28, during a 75-minute window opening at 8:15 a.m. Eastern time. The attempt would be the first designed to place the vehicle into Earth orbit; its 13 previous test flights followed suborbital trajectories. The planned mission calls for Starship to fly for nearly 10 hours, complete about six orbits of Earth at roughly 275 kilometers altitude and deploy 26 next-generation Starlink satellites before a planned splashdown in the Pacific Ocean west of Chile. The Federal Aviation Administration issued a launch and re-entry license on Sept. 26. Articles published before the scheduled launch did not report whether the attempt succeeded.
science.image_alt: SpaceX targets first Starship orbital flight on 14th test flight

science.title: Fossils trace oxygen’s role and early human movement
science.summary: A study comparing fossil limb bones identified differences in movement between Australopithecus and early Homo. Australopithecus combined upright walking with substantial time in trees, while early Homo had relatively stronger thigh bones than arm bones, consistent with more ground-based movement. Separately, researche
science.content: A study comparing fossil limb bones identified differences in movement between Australopithecus and early Homo. Australopithecus combined upright walking with substantial time in trees, while early Homo had relatively stronger thigh bones than arm bones, consistent with more ground-based movement. Separately, researchers analyzed more than 12,000 microscopic fossils from ancient rocks in northern Australia and found early eukaryotes in oxygenated settings ranging from coastal mudflats to the open sea, but not in oxygen-free samples. The fossils date from about 1.75 billion to 1.4 billion years ago; the study appeared in Nature.
science.image_alt: Fossils trace oxygen’s role and early human movement

sports.title: American cyclist Brandon McNulty wins 2026 road world title with solo breakaway
sports.summary: Brandon McNulty of the United States won the men’s road race at the UCI Road World Championships in Montreal on September 27, breaking clear with about 32 kilometres remaining and finishing the 273.4-kilometre race in 6 hours, 17 minutes and 4 seconds. He beat Australia’s Michael Matthews by 13 seconds, while Dutch for
sports.content: Brandon McNulty of the United States won the men’s road race at the UCI Road World Championships in Montreal on September 27, breaking clear with about 32 kilometres remaining and finishing the 273.4-kilometre race in 6 hours, 17 minutes and 4 seconds. He beat Australia’s Michael Matthews by 13 seconds, while Dutch former champion Mathieu van der Poel took third. McNulty became the first American men’s road world champion since Lance Armstrong in 1993. The 28-year-old UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider succeeded his teammate Tadej Pogačar, who missed the race after a crash at the Vuelta a España. McNulty attacked after a volatile series of moves and regrouping among the leading contenders and held off the chase despite his advantage narrowing on the final lap.
sports.image_alt: American cyclist Brandon McNulty wins 2026 road world title with solo breakaway

sports.title: MLB sets 12-team postseason bracket for 2026
sports.summary: Major League Baseball’s 2026 regular season ended on September 27, setting the 12-team playoff field. Houston secured the American League West after Texas lost its finale, while Philadelphia beat Tampa Bay 7-3 to claim the National League’s final wild-card spot. The first-round matchups are White Sox at Astros and Red
sports.content: Major League Baseball’s 2026 regular season ended on September 27, setting the 12-team playoff field. Houston secured the American League West after Texas lost its finale, while Philadelphia beat Tampa Bay 7-3 to claim the National League’s final wild-card spot. The first-round matchups are White Sox at Astros and Red Sox at Yankees in the AL, and Phillies at Braves and Cubs at Padres in the NL. The Rays, Guardians, Brewers and Dodgers earned first-round byes. All four Wild Card Series are best-of-three and begin September 29. The Division Series follow, and World Series Game 7 is scheduled for October 31.

sports.title: Rain sends India, Pakistan into Asian Games cricket semifinals
sports.summary: Persistent rain in Nisshin, Japan, washed out both men’s cricket quarter-finals on Monday, September 28, before a ball was bowled. Defending champion India advanced over Afghanistan and Pakistan progressed past Hong Kong under a tournament rule that sends the higher-ranked side through when a knockout match has no resu
sports.content: Persistent rain in Nisshin, Japan, washed out both men’s cricket quarter-finals on Monday, September 28, before a ball was bowled. Defending champion India advanced over Afghanistan and Pakistan progressed past Hong Kong under a tournament rule that sends the higher-ranked side through when a knockout match has no result; India is No. 1 in the ICC T20I rankings, while Afghanistan is No. 10. India will face the winner of the Nepal-Sri Lanka quarter-final, while Pakistan will meet the winner of Bangladesh-Malaysia. The semi-finals are scheduled for Thursday.
sports.image_alt: Rain sends India, Pakistan into Asian Games cricket semifinals

sports.title: Chelsea beat Arsenal 1-0 as Thompson settles WSL derby
sports.summary: Chelsea beat Arsenal 1-0 at Stamford Bridge on September 27, with Alyssa Thompson scoring the only goal in the 39th minute. Chelsea moved level with Tottenham and to within two points of leaders Manchester City, extending their Women’s Super League unbeaten run to 12 matches. Arsenal threatened early, hitting the post
sports.content: Chelsea beat Arsenal 1-0 at Stamford Bridge on September 27, with Alyssa Thompson scoring the only goal in the 39th minute. Chelsea moved level with Tottenham and to within two points of leaders Manchester City, extending their Women’s Super League unbeaten run to 12 matches. Arsenal threatened early, hitting the post twice, then pushed for an equaliser after the break; Chelsea held on for the win.
sports.image_alt: Chelsea beat Arsenal 1-0 as Thompson settles WSL derby

sports.title: South Africa beats Australia to clinch ODI series
sports.summary: South Africa beat Australia by 32 runs in Johannesburg on September 27, taking an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match one-day international series. South Africa made 365-9, led by David Miller’s 142 from 93 balls and captain Temba Bavuma’s 103 from 116. Their fourth-wicket partnership added 156. Australia were dis
sports.content: South Africa beat Australia by 32 runs in Johannesburg on September 27, taking an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match one-day international series. South Africa made 365-9, led by David Miller’s 142 from 93 balls and captain Temba Bavuma’s 103 from 116. Their fourth-wicket partnership added 156. Australia were dismissed for 333 in 49.5 overs. Australia’s Mitchell Marsh and Travis Head each made 84 and added 130 for the first wicket, but South Africa took regular wickets after their dismissals and held on despite Xavier Bartlett’s 50 from 28 balls. The result secured the series with one match remaining. The third ODI is scheduled for September 30 in Potchefstroom.
sports.image_alt: South Africa beats Australia to clinch ODI series

sports.title: USC suspends linebacker after Oregon quarterback concussion
sports.summary: USC suspended linebacker Desman Stephens II for one game on Sunday, Sept. 27, after he hit Oregon quarterback Dante Moore late and celebrated while Moore received medical attention during Oregon’s 41-27 win on Saturday. Officials ejected Stephens for targeting after he struck Moore as the quarterback slid during a seco
sports.content: USC suspended linebacker Desman Stephens II for one game on Sunday, Sept. 27, after he hit Oregon quarterback Dante Moore late and celebrated while Moore received medical attention during Oregon’s 41-27 win on Saturday. Officials ejected Stephens for targeting after he struck Moore as the quarterback slid during a second-quarter scramble. Moore was taken from the field by ambulance and diagnosed with a concussion. Oregon coach Dan Lanning said Moore’s MRI and CT scans revealed no additional injuries and did not provide a timetable for his return. Stephens apologized, calling his reaction “completely inappropriate and inexcusable,” while USC coach Lincoln Riley said the conduct was unacceptable and did not reflect the program.
sports.image_alt: USC suspends linebacker after Oregon quarterback concussion

sports.title: Kohli reaches 15,000 ODI runs in India
sports.summary: Virat Kohli scored an unbeaten 139 from 88 balls, his record-extending 55th ODI century, as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the opening match of their three-match series in Thiruvananthapuram on September 27. India reached 300 for two in 41.4 overs while chasing 296, with Kohli and captain Shubman Gill, who
sports.content: Virat Kohli scored an unbeaten 139 from 88 balls, his record-extending 55th ODI century, as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the opening match of their three-match series in Thiruvananthapuram on September 27. India reached 300 for two in 41.4 overs while chasing 296, with Kohli and captain Shubman Gill, who scored 110, leading the successful chase. Kohli crossed 15,000 ODI runs, becoming the second batter to reach the mark after Sachin Tendulkar. He did so in his 303rd ODI innings.
sports.image_alt: Kohli reaches 15,000 ODI runs in India

sports.title: Manchester City found guilty of 114 Premier League charges
sports.summary: An independent commission reviewed allegations concerning Manchester City’s finances from 2009 to 2018, as well as separate charges over the club’s cooperation with the Premier League’s investigation. Neither the league nor City has publicly confirmed the reported verdict, and the written decision has not been released
sports.content: An independent commission reviewed allegations concerning Manchester City’s finances from 2009 to 2018, as well as separate charges over the club’s cooperation with the Premier League’s investigation. Neither the league nor City has publicly confirmed the reported verdict, and the written decision has not been released. City denies wrongdoing and says the legal process is ongoing. The club is expected to appeal after the commission determines sanctions; reported potential outcomes include a fine, points deduction or expulsion from the Premier League. The appeal and any subsequent court action could prolong the case, with Sky Sports reporting that a final resolution may take years.
sports.image_alt: Manchester City found guilty of 114 Premier League charges
